When the prior is weak and the sample is moderate or large,
the posterior mean from a well-mixed chain
and the [maximum likelihood estimate](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-mle)
typically agree closely,
and the posterior standard deviation is close to the frequentist
[standard error](estimation.qmd#def-SE)
[@dobson4e, Chapter 13, p. 302].
As $n$ grows the likelihood dominates the prior,
so the posterior concentrates near the maximum likelihood estimate.
Comparing the two is therefore a useful check on an MCMC analysis.
